To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the variability of the centre pressure movement during gat in young and middle-age women is significantly higher in selected subphases of stance in the older women.
the COP movement variability is greater in the elder group compared with the younger one and that the PS and LR subphases are the most unstable during gait.
the COP variability is higher in the elder group than in the younger group, especially during the PS, LR, MSt and TSt subphases, and the COP variability is the highest during the PS and LR subphases.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the variability of COP displacement during gait in healthy young and middle-aged females.
the variability of the COP movement during walking.
the age-related variability of COP movement during walking, which is important in fall risk assessment.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the elder group showed a higher variability of the COP movement in all stance phases of gait, except the terminal stance phase.
the variability of COP displacement during walking is higher in middle-aged women, and the highest values were found in the LR and PS sub-phases.
the variability of COP displacement during gait is higher in older women than in younger women.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
middle-aged females have a higher variability of COP movement in the PS subphase, which is related to balance and fall risk.
the variability of COP displacement during gait in healthy middle-aged women was higher compared with young women.
the COP movement variability in the PS, the LR and the MSt subphase was significantly higher in the elder group than in the younger group.
The main takeaway from our work is that
COP displacement variability is higher in middle-aged women during walking.
the variability parameters of COP movement are higher in the middle-aged group compared with the younger one.
COP movement variability is higher in the elder group than in the younger group.
